top.resumen_es: U.S. forces have helped Persian Gulf producers move more than 1.5 billion barrels out of the Strait of Hormuz since the Iran war began, Adm. top.titulo: India's Stock Market Feels the Heat From High Oil Prices
top.resumen_es: The latest jump in oil prices has disturbed Indian equities, with both major indices starting the week with losses and 12 out of India’s 16 sectors booking losses, Reuters reported earlier in the day. With Brent crude trading at over $114 per barrel, it is not hard to see why investor sentiment in the world’s third-largest importer of crude is not exactly optimistic, pushing Sensex down by 0.46 today, and Nifty 50 down by 0.5. top.titulo: Saudi Arabia Turns to Singapore for Oil Storage
top.resumen_es: Saudi Arabia has struck a deal with the Singaporean government to store crude oil in underground caverns in the city-state, Bloomberg reported today. The report follows the latest Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure over the weekend, which included oil facilities among their targets. The Saudi crude will be stored in the Jurong Rock Caverns, which are part of a petrochemical complex in southern Singapore, with deliveries to the caverns set to begin in the second half of next year. top.titulo: Oil Prices Dip but Hold Above $100 as Middle East Supply Threats Mount
top.resumen_es: Crude oil prices began trading with a dip this week but remain significantly elevated as hostilities between Yemen’s Houthis and Saudi Arabia, as well as Iranian attacks on tankers in the Persian Gulf, continue.
